notes: The grounding Phase N6's recalibration-guidance feature will be graded on. The EPA SOP added on 2026-08-21 covers calibration of exactly the six parameters the DataPod measures and is the only document in the corpus with per-parameter post-calibration drift criteria — the numbers a recalibration recommendation would have to cite. It also states the deployment pattern this fleet actually runs: continuous instruments are calibrated before deployment and checked on recovery. Both sources are outside the ◆G9 slice, so direct-feed is expected to refuse. NOTE: this document is scanned and its text comes from OCR; the criteria table reads cleanly but the plus/minus signs render as bare '+' in places.

turns.content: We pull the pods every autumn after about nine months in the water. What are we actually supposed to check when one comes out?

must_contain: states that a continuously monitoring instrument is calibrated before deployment and its calibration is checked on recovery to determine whether it drifted
gives the mechanics of the check: put the instrument in measurement mode, not calibration mode, read the standards used at the initial calibration, and compare against the initial calibration values
states that if the check falls outside the criteria the measurement data must be qualified
states the result is recorded in the calibration log with the instrument, the standards used and their source, the date, the readings, the post-calibration check and who performed it
must_not: describes recalibrating the instrument before recording the recovery check
invents a post-deployment procedure absent from the corpus
presents an Atlas datasheet's recalibration interval as the post-deployment check
rubric.notes: EPA SOP §4.0 and §6.0. The 'measurement mode, not calibration mode' detail is the one that separates a real reading of the SOP from a plausible paraphrase — recalibrating first destroys the evidence of drift.

turns.content: What counts as drifted, though? Give me the numbers per parameter.

must_contain: dissolved oxygen: ±0.5 mg/L of the saturation value, and below 0.5 mg/L for the zero-DO solution but not a negative value
specific conductance: ±5 percent of the standard or ±10 µS/cm, whichever is greater
pH: ±0.3 pH unit against the pH 7 buffer
states these are the defaults used only when the project's quality-assurance project plan or sampling and analysis plan does not specify its own criteria
must_not: invents a criterion for a parameter the SOP does not list
presents the USGS stabilization criteria for recording a reading as post-calibration drift criteria
omits the conditional and presents the numbers as universal
rubric.notes: EPA SOP §6.0 criteria table. The last must_contain is the trap: the stabilization criteria in NFM A6.0 table 6.0–1 (±0.2 °C, ±0.2 mg/L, ±0.1 pH unit, ±5 µS/cm or ±3 %, ±0.5 TU or ±5 %) look similar and mean something entirely different. An answer that mixes the two tables is wrong even though every number in it exists in the corpus.
